firmware.note: firmware/status serves a minimal envelope until a check has run since boot, then a state-dependent superset (~26 top-level keys, we model 12); the unmodelled remainder is exempted wholesale so canary results do not depend on when the box last ran a check. downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages are now modelled as count gauges (#237). The 26.7 full-inventory keys (all_packages/all_sets) remain a #227 opportunity - deliberately NOT decoded, so raw composite inventories never become per-package metrics (#373 scope). connection/repository/remove_packages/upgrade_sets/download_size were REMOVED from this list on 2026-07-25: #373 models connection/repository as bounded update-check state and remove_packages/upgrade_sets as count gauges, and #380 models download_size as a byte gauge, so they are no longer unmodelled. upgrade_packages[].size is BOX STATE, not drift: core's check.sh builds an ordinary package-upgrade entry as name/repository/current_version/new_version with no size key at all (check.sh:271-281), and emits size only on the synthetic base and kernel entries, each guarded on opnsense-update reporting a non-empty size (check.sh:328-337, 350-359). FirmwareController.php:133 reads it back behind !empty()+is_numeric(), so upstream itself treats it as optional. The field therefore appears only while a BASE OR KERNEL upgrade is pending; a box with only ordinary package upgrades legitimately omits it. Exempting rather than fixing the testbed is safe here because size backs no exported metric - it is parsed into firmware.go's UpgradePackages struct but never copied into FirmwarePackageUpgrade, so the canary blinds us to nothing consumed. PRUNE TRIGGER: if size is ever consumed by a metric, delete this entry and instead hold a pending base/kernel upgrade on the testbed so the path is genuinely covered MINIMAL-ENVELOPE ADDITIONS 2026-07-25 (#373/#380): connection, repository, download_size, remove_packages, upgrade_sets, downgrade_packages and reinstall_packages are ALL state-dependent top-level keys that exist only AFTER a check has been stored. Verified live the same day: the dev box served the full 26-key superset at 18:33, then reverted to the bare 3-key envelope (product/status/status_msg, status=none) after a package operation cleared the stored check - and the canary flagged all seven as Missing. This is BOX STATE, not drift, exactly like the pre-existing entries above. downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages were a latent gap from #237 that only became visible once a run caught the box pre-check. The remove_packages[].* and upgrade_sets[].* prefixes cover the element paths for the same reason. PRUNE TRIGGER: none - this is permanent box state, since a box that has never run a check since boot is a legitimate and reachable state. The exporter handles it by presence-gating on CheckPresent, so no success/state series is fabricated; that gating was live-confirmed by this very reversion. knownExtraPaths (#457): the whole nested `product` object (opnsense/firmware.go's firmwareStatusResponse.Product) is exempted. product.CORE_* is a pkg-static shell-variable-style build banner (abi/arch/commit/copyright/maintainer/etc.) - pure identity metadata, the same class already exempted wholesale at the top level. product.product_* (excluding product_check) mirrors the already-modeled top-level product identity fields (product_id/product_version/product_abi/...) plus extra GUI/vendor metadata (license, mirror, website, tier) that has no top-level twin - config/identity, no metric use. product.product_check.* is, field-for-field, an exact name match to data already decoded at the TOP LEVEL of this same response (connection/download_size/repository/remove_packages/upgrade_sets/downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages/last_check/needs_reboot/os_version/product_id/product_version/product_abi/new_packages/upgrade_packages) or to the top-level knownExtraTopKeys already acknowledged above (api_version/product_target/upgrade_major_message/upgrade_major_version) - strongly indicating OPNsense nests the full stored check result a second time under product.product_check rather than serving distinct data, the same pattern as the pre-existing product.product_check.upgrade_needs_reboot entry already modeled. This is inferred from field-name structure, not a live byte-for-byte diff of the two locations - if that is ever disproved, split this entry apart. (fixup) product.product_abi/product.product_arch were missed from the product.* enumeration in the first pass - same reasoning as the rest of product.product_*: identity metadata mirroring the already-modeled top-level product_abi field, no metric use. MOVED TOP-KEY -> MISSINGOK 2026-07-31 (#583): upgrade_major_version and the TOP-LEVEL upgrade_needs_reboot are now decoded (firmwareStatusResponse), so they leave knownExtraTopKeys; they join missingOK for the same reason as every other state-dependent key above - check.sh writes them into the stored check's JSON heredoc unconditionally (stable/26.7 and stable/26.1 lines 422-423), so they exist in the superset and are absent only in the pre-check minimal envelope. PRUNE TRIGGER: none - permanent box state. upgrade_major_version is $(opnsense-update -vR) assigned only inside `if [ -n "${packages_is_size}" ]` (line 366), so an EMPTY STRING is the 'no major upgrade offered' signal and emptiness is the availability test. Note the exporter already exported upgrade_needs_reboot from the NESTED product.product_check copy; it now prefers the top-level key and falls back to the nested one. That is safe because the duplicate-representation claim in the product.* note above is no longer an inference: FirmwareController.php:126-127 literally does `$response = $product['product_check']; $response['product'] = $product;`, i.e. the top level IS product_check and `product` re-serves the same object. Source-verified 2026-07-31 on both stable branches - the 'if that is ever disproved, split this entry apart' caveat above is hereby discharged, not disproved. A box that has never run a firmware check since boot serves ONLY the bare three-key envelope (product / status / status_msg) with no top-level identity keys and no last_check at all, so the old top-level-only read left opnsense_firmware_info publishing 'undefined' for all four identity labels on the default post-reboot state. Resolution is now top-level-wins-else-nested per the chase pattern, so a checked box is unchanged. product.product_arch and product.product_series stay unmodelled and stay listed.

(1) flatsize is NOT 'size in bytes': scripts/firmware/query.sh:52 queries pkg with %sh, pkg's HUMANIZED size, and Core/Api/FirmwareController.php:854 then passes it through formatBytes(), which returns any non-numeric input unchanged (lines 55-58) - so the wire value is a formatted base-2 string ('168KiB', '1.2MiB'), parsed by parseFirmwarePluginSize with the same unit table as the firmware download_size field. Decoding 'N/A' as false is therefore a decode of a known-false value, not a guess. plugin[].configured stays exempted - it is derived (name in config plugin list OR automatic==1), so it adds nothing over the two flags now modeled. hasyncServices.note: rows[].running is a DEFENSIVE ALIAS in hasyncServiceRow (opnsense/hasync.go) that upstream has never populated on any release, so it can never be present on any box - this is NOT box-state and NOT drift. Source: list_services_xmlrpc in the HA XML-RPC surface builds each row with 'status' and no 'running' key. #460 built a real HA peer (a second OPNsense on the isolated testbed bridge) and confirmed on 2026-07-28 against a live 38-row response that the key is absent from a configured, reachable, fully-populated payload - the strongest available evidence, because it excludes every other reason a path can be missing (no peer configured, peer unreachable, empty rows). Without this entry the canary reports it on every run forever. PRUNE TRIGGER: remove this entry when the 'running' alias is removed from hasyncServiceRow, OR if upstream ever starts emitting it - in which case the effective-running expression should prefer it and this entry becomes wrong in the other direction. TestFetchHasyncStatus_RunningAliasNeverOnTheWire pins the alias inert in the meantime: if that expression is ever 'simplified' to prefer running, every stopped service on every real box silently flips to 1. --- knownExtraPaths (#480): all eight are REDUNDANT, triaged per key against upstream source on 2026-07-28. They are new only because #460 gave the box a real HA peer, so rows[] was non-empty for the first time - upstream did not change. Chain: HasyncStatusController::servicesAction -> configd 'system ha services_cached' -> ha_xmlrpc_exec.php services -> XML-RPC opnsense.list_services -> list_services_xmlrpc (src/etc/inc/xmlrpc/service.inc), which iterates plugins_services() and adds only 'status' itself. configd/php/mwexec are the three ALTERNATIVE SERVICE-CONTROL DISPATCH TABLES (start/stop/restart command names, PHP callbacks, raw shell), consumed only by service_control_start/stop/restart in src/etc/inc/util.inc - internal wiring, and exposing raw command or PHP-function strings as label data would be an info leak with no operator value. pidfile is the INPUT to the liveness check (service_status reads isvalidpid($service['pidfile']), util.inc) whose OUTPUT is the 'status' we already model. nocheck short-circuits service_status to always-true (util.inc), so its effect is ALREADY BAKED INTO the running gauge we export - modelling it separately would double-count a static per-service definition. locked only gates whether the webConfigurator renders start/stop/restart buttons (hasync_status.volt) - UI permission, not health. dns_ports is a resolver-port-conflict input for service_by_filter, set only on the unbound/dnsmasq rows; if that data is ever wanted it belongs to the Unbound/Dnsmasq collectors reading their own config endpoints, not to a remote-peer HA service list. uid is synthesized by the controller itself as name[_id] (HasyncStatusController.php) purely as a bootgrid row key - it is exactly the name+id composite the exporter already derives for series identity. PRESENCE IS CONDITIONAL: only uid is on every row; the other seven are set only by the plugin _services() functions that declare them, so these paths are stable in shape but not in per-row presence. PRUNE TRIGGER: none of these becomes interesting unless upstream repurposes one to carry health state - re-triage if the note above stops matching the source. --- rows[].verbose ADDED (#496 nightly, plugins_services() chain confirmed identical to the #480 batch): verified against opnsense/core master, src/etc/inc/plugins.inc.d/dpinger.inc, dpinger_services() (the gateway-monitor/dpinger service, one row per configured gateway plus a synthetic 'Gateway Watcher' entry) - it hardcodes $pconfig['verbose'] = false and lists 'verbose' in php.args alongside 'id'; this is a static PHP-restart-callback argument (verbosity of the reconfigure log output), not runtime health or state, same PRESENCE IS CONDITIONAL bucket as the other seven plugin-declared keys above - it surfaced only now because the nightly testbed has gateway monitoring configured, and no prior canary run happened to include a dpinger row. PRUNE TRIGGER: none, unless upstream repurposes this static flag.

hasyncVersion.note: KEPT, and its old note was MISLEADING. It read 'present only for some HA peer states; box has no HA peer', which implies a real peer would produce these keys. It does not. #460 built a real HA peer (a second OPNsense on the isolated testbed bridge) and confirmed on 2026-07-28 that 'status' and 'message' are absent from the configured-AND-reachable response too: they are the EXCEPTION envelope, not a peer state. Source, from the installed scripts/system/ha_xmlrpc_exec.php on the testbed and identical on master: the 'version' action echoes json_encode(['response' => $payload]) with no 'status' and no 'message' on every success path; the only branches that emit them are the catch(Exception) handler (['status'=>'error','message'=>$e->getMessage()]) and an unknown-action default the controller can never reach, since versionAction always passes 'version'. Both were observed live: with the peer's link down the endpoint returned exactly {"status":"error","message":"fetch error. remote host down? ..."}. So these two keys are present ONLY when the XML-RPC call throws, which is the branch FetchHasyncStatus deliberately maps to Reachable=false. PRUNE TRIGGER: only if upstream moves the version payload onto the ['response'=>..., 'status'=>'ok'] shape the stop/start/restart actions already use - at which point 'status' becomes unconditional and this entry is wrong in the other direction. A third live shape belongs on the record here because no fixture had it before #460: when the peer is reachable but the XML-RPC credentials are wrong, the client does NOT throw - the endpoint answers {"response":"Authentication failed"}, a JSON STRING where the success path serves an object. That still carries neither 'status' nor 'message'.

healthCheck.note: Two unrelated things. (1) The CrashReporter/Firewall/System entries are the legacy pre-25.1 health shape, killed by upstream refactor 1fc5a6335 (2024-12-12). They are ALREADY outside the current+previous support window (26.1 + 25.7), so the trigger has fired — but pruning them is not a ledger edit: the exemptions only exist because the structs do, and deleting the structs drops support for pre-25.1 boxes, which is a product decision rather than canary hygiene. Left in place deliberately; raise an issue if that support should end (#284). (2) 'subsystems' is BOX STATE, not a version prune: SystemController::statusAction() only assigns $response['subsystems'] inside `if ($statuses)`, so a box with no subsystem reporting anything omits the key entirely. Verified 2026-07-17 against upstream source (blob ea83f28a is IDENTICAL on master, stable/26.1 and stable/25.7, unchanged since 2025-01-21) and against a live healthy box. It reappears the moment any subsystem reports, which is why #235 flagged it and #243 did not. metadata.subsystems is NOT populated on any release and is no longer modelled — see #284. knownExtraPaths (#376): the 26.1+ metadata block carries four keys we deliberately do not model. metadata.subsystems is the phantom generation from #284 - upstream never populates it on any release and it was removed from the structs; PRUNE TRIGGER: only if upstream ever populates it with data worth exporting. metadata.translations is GUI i18n text. metadata.System.message/.title are free-form GUI strings; only metadata.System.status is consumed. PRUNE TRIGGER for those three: if a metric ever needs them. Paths are spelled in the STRUCT's casing (System) even though 26.1 serves lowercase 'system' - the validator canonicalizes to the schema spelling on purpose, so the exemption matches every release's casing BATCH 4 (#613, nightly only, 2026-07-31T14:10Z run): subsystems.*.{age,isBanner,location,persistent,priority,timestamp,title} - the seven unmodelled siblings of the message/status/statusCode that HealthCheckSubsystem (opnsense/health_check.go) does model. NOT a #284 contradiction: #284's phantom was metadata.subsystems, which upstream still never populates; the TOP-LEVEL subsystems map is real, and these are its per-notice fields. Verified against the producing source, SystemStatus::collectStatus() (mvc/app/library/OPNsense/System/SystemStatus.php, core master 2026-07-31), which builds a FIXED nine-key record per subsystem - title/statusCode/message/location/timestamp/persistent/isBanner/priority/scope - every one of them unconditional, plus SystemController::statusAction()'s two additions. That source also settles the nightly-only asymmetry far more crisply than this entry's older wording: collectStatus() does `if ($obj->getStatus() == SystemStatusCode::OK) { continue; }`, so a subsystem is emitted ONLY while it is NOT OK. An all-healthy box therefore serves an empty map by construction, and the nightly box simply has a subsystem complaining. It also explains why `scope` never appears in a finding despite being in the record: statusAction() unsets it before returning. Field by field - title is a translated display label and location is a GUI page path, both identity; persistent and isBanner are booleans of GUI presentation (statusAction() uses isBanner itself, to exclude banners from the metadata.System roll-up we already consume); priority is the integer tie-breaker for the controller's own uasort within a status code, ordering metadata rather than a quantity; age is a LOCALISED HUMAN STRING ('5 minutes ago', '2 days ago') that statusAction() derives from timestamp via gettext/sprintf and emits only when timestamp is non-empty - translated prose, never a metric. OPPORTUNITY: subsystems.*.timestamp is the one genuine candidate - a Unix epoch, unconditional in collectStatus(), and locale-independent, so 'how long has this subsystem been unhealthy' is a real gauge that `age` cannot back. PRUNE TRIGGER: remove timestamp from this list if that gauge is ever added. CAVEAT worth knowing before reading a missing subsystem as box state: statusAction() ACL-filters this map - a subsystem whose `location` page the API credential cannot access is dropped from the response entirely (isPageAccessible, SystemController.php:87-92). Absence here can therefore be a CREDENTIAL property, not only a healthy box.

Kernel bookkeeping (id/pid/refcnt/seq/sadb_seq), the anti-replay window size, and the ESP/AH algorithm names are identity/config, not metric-worthy; addtime_created/addtime_current are redundant wall-clock forms of the already-modeled addtime_diff age. PRUNE TRIGGER for the usetime_* trio: a real deployment configuring margintime. PLACEHOLDER EXEMPTION RETIRED 2026-08-01 (#618): a prod-scoped missingOK used to carry reqid/state/addtime_diff+hard+soft and bytes_current+hard+soft/allocated+hard+soft, eleven paths absent for one reason - the box had no SA, so the only row was setkey's synthetic "No SAD entries." line. cmd/apidrift was the sole consumer that read that row as data; FetchIPsecSAD has always discarded it. The probe now discards it too, via the SAME predicate (IsIPsecSADPlaceholderRow, opnsense/ipsec.go), so an empty SADB validates as zero rows and all eleven paths stay ENFORCED on every profile including prod - which is the point, since six of them back opnsense_ipsec_sa_bytes_* / _allocated_*. quaggaBfdNeighbors.note: frrBFDNeighborEntry (opnsense/frr.go) models peer/local/interface/status/uptime. FIRST LEDGER ENTRY (#480) - this endpoint was previously unledgered, so it reported on every run. THE UPSTREAM FOR THIS ENDPOINT IS FRR, NOT OPNSENSE: actions_quagga.conf's [diagnostics.bfd_neighbors] runs `vtysh -c 'show bfd peers json'` and DiagnosticsController::bfdTreeFetch only re-keys the array by peer, so every field name here is FRR bfdd's own and a future 'did upstream change' question must be answered against FRR releases, not OPNsense ones. All three missingOK paths are BOX-STATE, verified directly in FRR's bfdd/bfdd_vty.c rather than inferred: 'uptime' is emitted only inside the PTM_BFD_UP branch of the session-state switch and 'downtime' only inside PTM_BFD_DOWN (they are mutually exclusive, and PTM_BFD_INIT/PTM_BFD_ADM_DOWN emit neither); 'local' is emitted only when the session's local address is not all-zero; 'interface' only when key.ifname is non-empty, which is the single-hop case (the 'multihop' extra key on this same response shows this box has multihop sessions). None of the three is drift and none is a code change. knownExtraPaths buckets: id/remote-id/vrf/multihop/type/log-session-changes/passive-mode are session identity and config bookkeeping; detect-multiplier/detection-timeout and the receive/transmit interval family (local and remote) are negotiated timer CONFIG that changes on reconfiguration, not on link health; the echo-*-interval family is inert unless BFD echo mode is enabled. OPPORTUNITIES, exempted here so the canary can go quiet but tracked as real modelling gaps: 'diagnostic'/'remote-diagnostic' carry FRR's bounded down-REASON enum (diag2str: 'Control Detection Time Expired', 'Echo Function Failed', ...), which is distinct from the up/down state we already export and is the single most useful field in this list; 'rtt-avg'/'rtt-min'/'rtt-max' are per-peer round-trip gauges, one series each on an already-modelled peer, zero unless both ends support FRR's RTT extension; 'downtime' is the Down-state counterpart of the modelled uptime, so a peer that is down currently reports no duration at all. MODELLED 2026-07-28 (#484) and removed from this list: diagnostic and remote-diagnostic (labels on opnsense_frr_bfd_peer_diagnostic_info), the rtt-* trio (opnsense_frr_bfd_peer_rtt_{min,avg,max}_microseconds - FRR reports these in MICROSECONDS, confirmed by bfdd_vty.c's own human-readable 'RTT min/avg/max: %u/%u/%u usec'), and downtime (opnsense_frr_bfd_peer_downtime_seconds). The downtime gauge is emitted ONLY when FRR sends the key, never defaulted to 0: Downtime is decoded into a *float64 so absent is distinguishable from a genuine 0, because a peer that has just gone down legitimately reports 0 seconds and an INIT/ADM_DOWN peer reports nothing at all. Do not 'simplify' that pointer away. Also corrected here: the diag2str value set is lowercase ('ok', 'control detection time expired', 'neighbor signaled session down', ...) per bfdd/bfd.c - an earlier fixture used an invented 'no-diagnostic'. PRUNE TRIGGER: the remaining keys stay until FRR stops emitting them; the echo-* family becomes worth modelling only if echo mode is ever run on a monitored box.

THIS ENDPOINT'S CANARY FINDING WAS A CODE BUG, NOT AN EXEMPTION, and the fix has landed: the struct tagged the last two fields 'session-up-events'/'session-down-events', which is why the canary reported those two as MISSING while reporting 'session-up'/'session-down' as unexpected EXTRAS on the same response. firewallStates.note: #603: the pf state table is read for ONE thing - route-to, the egress device pf actually applied - so the row struct models only the pre-NAT 5-tuple, the direction and route-to. Everything listed here is deliberately unmodelled and each is a decision, not an oversight. IDENTITY: id, label, rule, descr, iface, interface (the rule and interface this state was created by; unbounded, and the exporter already exports firewall rule metrics from firewallRules). VOLUME: bytes and pkts are per-state [in,out] pairs, which is the same traffic ng_netflow already exports per flow - counting it twice from two sources with no way to reconcile them is exactly what #346 decision 3 exists to avoid. LIFECYCLE: age, expires, state (the TCP state string). NAT: nat_addr/nat_port were pruned from this list on 2026-08-01 and are now MODELLED (#623). The note here used to say they were "the post-NAT binding" and that no NAT join was ever needed - BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG. Verified live on 2026-08-01: on a direction="out" row nat_addr/nat_port hold the PRE-NAT endpoint, so the row states pf's own translation mapping. That is not needed for #603 (the direction="in" row is indeed the pre-NAT view for route-to purposes) but it is exactly what #623 needs: ng_netflow exports a NAT'd conversation twice, once pre-NAT on the LAN node and once post-NAT on the WAN node, and without this mapping the two copies cannot be recognised as one conversation - which was double-counting a policy-routed WAN by 38.5%. ROUTING: gateway is null on every row observed live (the routing decision travels in route-to), flags is a small array of pf state flags, ipproto is the address family, and reply-to is route-to's inbound twin, present on 126 of 6,602 rows and not the direction this repair acts on. OPPORTUNITY, if any of it is ever wanted: a per-state-table breakdown by TCP state or by rule would be a genuine metric, and reply-to would extend the repair to inbound policy routing.
